title: LVLM-EHub: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Large Vision-Language Models
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

01_initial_request.target_name: LVLM-eHub, a comprehensive evaluation hub and online arena for publicly available large vision-language models
01_initial_request.input_data: Eight representative LVLM checkpoints with parameter sizes under 10B: BLIP2, LLaVA, LLaMA-Adapter V2, MiniGPT-4, mPLUG-Owl, Otter, InstructBLIP, and VPGTrans. Model metadata included visual encoders, LLM backbones, adaptation modules, visual tokens, tuning parameters, and training data scales: BLIP2 used 129M image-text pairs; LLaVA used 595K CC3M image-text samples and 158K LLaVA instruction samples; LLaMA-Adapter V2 used 200M LAION-400M image-text samples and 158K LLaVA instruction samples; MiniGPT-4 used 5M image-text samples and 3.5K CC+ChatGPT instruction samples; mPLUG-Owl used 204M image-text samples and 158K instruction samples; Otter used 158K instruction samples; InstructBLIP used 16M QA instruction samples; VPGTrans used 13.8M image-text samples and 3.5K instruction samples. The benchmark pool contained 47 text-related visual benchmarks grouped into 6 capability categories plus an online crowd-sourced arena.
01_initial_request.user_intent: Prior LVLM evaluations covered only specific tasks or subsets of models, so the authors wanted a holistic, comparable evaluation that could expose strengths, overfitting, hallucination, and open-world user-level behavior across representative LVLMs.
01_initial_request.quantifiable_goal: Evaluate 8 LVLMs with less than 10B parameters across 6 multimodal capability categories using 47 standard benchmarks, and provide an online anonymous pairwise arena with Elo-style rankings for open-world image/text chat.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] Recent LVLMs such as BLIP2, LLaVA, MiniGPT-4, mPLUG-Owl, Otter, InstructBLIP, and VPGTrans align visual encoders with LLMs and are increasingly used for multimodal QA and conversation. [Gap] Existing studies evaluated only limited capabilities such as hallucination, visual commonsense, OCR, or fine-grained perception, leaving no unified comparison across representative models. [Decision] Build a model zoo of public LVLMs and restrict the comparison to checkpoints below 10B parameters for fair and accessible evaluation.

tool.name: LVLM model survey and checkpoint collection

parameters.models: BLIP2, LLaVA, LLaMA-Adapter V2, MiniGPT-4, mPLUG-Owl, Otter, InstructBLIP, VPGTrans

02_agent_trajectory.observation: The authors assembled 8 LVLMs with diverse visual encoders, LLMs, adaptation modules, and training-data scales, including models trained with no visual instruction data, 3.5K instruction samples, 158K instruction samples, and 16M QA samples.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] LVLM behavior spans perception, text extraction, reasoning, commonsense, hallucination, and embodied planning. [Gap] A single task cannot reveal these different failure modes or allow a reliable model ranking. [Decision] Define 6 capability categories and collect 47 standard text-related visual benchmarks with specified evaluation splits.

parameters.capability_categories: visual perception; visual knowledge acquisition; visual reasoning; visual commonsense; object hallucination; embodied intelligence
parameters.example_visual_perception_sets: ImageNet1K 50K validation; CIFAR10 10K test; Pets37 3669 test; Flowers102 6149 test; COCO-OC 10000 validation; COCO-MCI 10000 validation; VCR-OC 10000 validation; VCR-MCI 1000 validation
parameters.example_reasoning_sets: DocVQA 5349 validation; TextVQA v0.5.1 5000 validation; STVQA 4000 train samples; OCR-VQA 100037 all; OKVQA 5046 validation; GQA 12578 testdev; Visdial 20640 validation QA pairs; SNLI-VE 500 dev

02_agent_trajectory.observation: The resulting benchmark hub covered image classification, object counting, multi-class identification, OCR, KIE, image captioning, VQA, knowledge-grounded image description, visual entailment, visual commonsense, POPE hallucination probing, and embodied-AI planning.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] LVLM outputs can be open-ended text, multiple-choice answers, yes/no answers, or plans, and existing metrics are not uniformly applicable. [Gap] A single evaluation interface would either over-constrain open-ended answers or fail to score structured tasks. [Decision] Use four zero-shot evaluation methods: question answering, prefix-based scoring, multi-turn reasoning, and user studies.

parameters.question_answering_prompt_example: "what is written in the image?" for OCR
parameters.prefix_based_score: select candidate answer with largest image-text prefix likelihood for multiple-choice QA
parameters.multi_turn_reasoning: LLM generates sub-questions; LVLM answers sub-questions; another LLM evaluates sub-answer quality iteratively
parameters.user_study_controls: randomly shuffle model output order and anonymize outputs

02_agent_trajectory.observation: The authors established task-specific scoring workflows using accuracy, word accuracy, entity-level F1, CIDEr, mean reciprocal rank, precision, recall, F1-score, yes-answer ratio, Elo rating, and human preference judgments depending on task type.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] Visual perception is a prerequisite for downstream LVLM reasoning and can be tested by recognizing categories, objects, and object counts. [Gap] It was unknown whether LVLMs could approach supervised vision systems in zero-shot perception. [Decision] Evaluate all 8 LVLMs on image classification, object counting, and multi-class identification using accuracy and normalized average scores.

parameters.datasets: ImageNet1K, CIFAR10, Pets37, Flowers102, COCO object counting, VCR object counting, COCO multi-class identification, VCR multi-class identification

02_agent_trajectory.observation: InstructBLIP obtained the best normalized average score of 0.928, followed by BLIP2 at 0.858 and mPLUG-Owl at 0.831. Individual zero-shot results remained far below supervised SOTA, for example the best LVLM ImageNet1K accuracy was 26.68% versus 91.10% supervised SOTA, and the best CIFAR10 accuracy was 67.96% versus 99.70% supervised SOTA.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] Visual knowledge acquisition requires reading text, extracting structured fields, and generating captions from images. [Gap] It was unclear how much visual encoders, Q-Former modules, and instruction tuning improve these zero-shot capabilities. [Decision] Evaluate OCR, KIE, and image captioning in a VQA-style framework using word accuracy, entity-level F1, and CIDEr.

parameters.OCR_datasets: IIIT5K, IC13, IC15, Total-Text, CUTE80, SVT, SVTP, COCO-Text, WordArt, CTW, HOST, WOST
parameters.metrics: word accuracy for OCR; entity-level F1 for KIE; CIDEr for image captioning

02_agent_trajectory.observation: InstructBLIP achieved the highest normalized average score of 0.967, BLIP2 scored 0.927, and VPGTrans scored 0.720. KIE performance was extremely weak relative to task-specific supervised systems, with SROIE and FUNSD LVLM scores around 0.01 to 2.16 while supervised SOTA was 97.81 and 89.45 respectively.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] Visual reasoning and commonsense require integrating image evidence, language, and background knowledge. [Gap] Open-ended generated content from instruction-tuned LVLMs may not be captured correctly by simple metrics, and hallucinated content can distort answers. [Decision] Evaluate VQA, knowledge-grounded image description, visual entailment, ImageNetVC, and VCR, using multi-turn reasoning where appropriate.

tool.name: Zero-shot visual reasoning and visual commonsense evaluation

parameters.reasoning_datasets: DocVQA, TextVQA, STVQA, OCR-VQA, OKVQA, GQA, Visdial, IconQA, VSR, WHOOPS, ScienceQA IMG, VizWiz, SNLI-VE
parameters.metrics: top-1 accuracy; MRR for Visdial; normalized average score

02_agent_trajectory.observation: For visual reasoning, InstructBLIP obtained the best normalized average score of 0.908, followed by LLaMA-Adapter V2 at 0.833 and LLaVA at 0.771. For visual commonsense, InstructBLIP scored 0.995 and LLaVA scored 0.791. Instruction-tuned LVLMs surpassed BLIP2 on SNLI-VE, where the final answer was obtained by multi-turn reasoning; InstructBLIP scored 59.00, LLaMA-Adapter V2 58.8, LLaVA 57.80, MiniGPT-4 54.80, mPLUG-Owl 54.50, Otter 52.60, VPGTrans 52.20, while BLIP2 scored 32.00.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] LVLMs can generate objects inconsistent with the image, a failure known as object hallucination. [Gap] Conventional captioning metrics such as CIDEr may not penalize hallucinated objects reliably. [Decision] Probe object hallucination on MSCOCO using the POPE multi-step yes/no QA pipeline with increasingly difficult negative-object sampling strategies.

parameters.metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ratio of answering Yes

02_agent_trajectory.observation: InstructBLIP performed best on the hallucination evaluation, followed by BLIP2; their average accuracy reached more than 80%. Instruction-tuned models except InstructBLIP performed worse than BLIP2 because they tended to answer Yes, indicating a tendency to hallucinate objects that were not present in the target image.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] Embodied intelligence tasks require converting visual observations and natural-language instructions into useful action plans. [Gap] Existing automatic metrics do not reliably judge plan relevance, conciseness, and usefulness. [Decision] Conduct anonymized and shuffled human user studies for embodied-AI planning outputs.

parameters.evaluation_controls: anonymous model outputs; randomly shuffled output order

02_agent_trajectory.observation: The user-study protocol allowed human assessment of generated plans in scenarios where automatic metrics were considered inadequate. The paper reports qualitative examples showing that some LVLM outputs identified task-relevant objects and produced stepwise plans, while others hallucinated scene elements or produced less actionable descriptions.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] Quantitative benchmarks are limited and may not represent open-world user interaction. [Gap] A model that scores highly on in-domain benchmarks may generalize poorly in free-form image/text chat. [Decision] Build LVLM Arena for anonymous randomized pairwise battles with human voting and Elo-style ranking.

parameters.sampling: random sampling from the model zoo
parameters.vote_options: Model A, Model B, Tie, Both are bad
parameters.chat_setting: single-round chats at the time of reporting
parameters.ranking_method: Elo rating updated from voting results

02_agent_trajectory.observation: Arena rankings changed as more evaluation samples were collected. InstructBLIP performed well on existing in-domain tasks but generalized poorly in the open-world arena, whereas instruction-tuned models with moderate high-quality instruction-following data such as mPLUG-Owl, MiniGPT-4, Otter, and LLaMA-Adapter V2 worked well in the open-world arena.

03_success_verification.validation_technique: The authors verified LVLM-eHub by running zero-shot quantitative evaluations on 47 benchmarks across 6 capability categories for 8 LVLMs, using task-appropriate metrics, and by deploying LVLM Arena for anonymous pairwise human preference evaluation with Elo-style ranking.

models_evaluated.interpretation: The benchmark covered 8 representative public LVLMs with checkpoints below 10B parameters.

capability_categories.interpretation: The suite covered visual perception, visual knowledge acquisition, visual reasoning, visual commonsense, object hallucination, and embodied intelligence.

standard_benchmarks.interpretation: The quantitative component consolidated 47 standard text-related visual benchmarks.

best_visual_perception_average_score.interpretation: InstructBLIP ranked highest in the visual perception category.

best_visual_knowledge_average_score.interpretation: InstructBLIP ranked highest across OCR, KIE, and captioning evaluations.

best_visual_reasoning_average_score.interpretation: InstructBLIP ranked highest across VQA, KGID, and visual entailment tasks.

best_visual_commonsense_average_score.interpretation: InstructBLIP ranked highest on ImageNetVC and VCR visual commonsense evaluation.

POPE_samples_per_split.interpretation: Each POPE hallucination split used 500 MSCOCO images with 6 questions per image.

embodied_user_study_participants.interpretation: Human evaluators judged embodied-planning outputs where automatic metrics were considered insufficient.

arena_ranking_snapshots.interpretation: The paper reported LVLM Arena rankings at least for June 3 and June 13, showing that rankings changed as more user votes were collected.

03_success_verification.final_verdict: The original goal was met: LVLM-eHub evaluated 8 representative LVLMs across 6 capability categories using 47 benchmarks and added an online open-world arena for human pairwise comparison. The evaluation produced concrete rankings and diagnostic findings, including strong in-domain performance but poor open-world generalization for InstructBLIP, large gaps between LVLMs and supervised SOTA on perception and KIE, and object hallucination in several instruction-tuned models.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: Zero-shot LVLM perception lagged far behind supervised vision systems.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: Even the best LVLM accuracies on coarse classification tasks were much lower than supervised SOTA, indicating that visual perception was not solved by the LVLM alignment and instruction-tuning pipelines.
04_failure_modes.correction: The authors reported the gap as a key diagnostic result and noted substantial room for improving LVLM perception ability.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: Key information extraction performance was extremely poor.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: LVLMs evaluated in a VQA-style zero-shot setup did not reliably extract structured fields from scanned receipts and forms; their SROIE and FUNSD scores were near zero to about 2.16 compared with supervised SOTA near 97.81 and 89.45.
04_failure_modes.correction: The authors retained KIE as part of the benchmark to expose this limitation rather than claiming the task was solved.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: Instruction-tuned LVLMs except InstructBLIP showed object hallucination.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: These models tended to answer Yes in POPE yes/no object-existence probing, causing them to assert the presence of objects that were absent from the image.
04_failure_modes.correction: The authors evaluated hallucination explicitly with POPE and reported that multi-turn reasoning could alleviate hallucination in related evaluations such as SNLI-VE and VCR.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: Conventional captioning metrics such as CIDEr could be ineffective under object hallucination.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: Generated captions may contain plausible but image-inconsistent objects, and a surface-level captioning score may not reliably penalize those hallucinated entities.
04_failure_modes.correction: The authors added a dedicated object-hallucination evaluation pipeline using POPE yes/no object probes.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: Strong in-domain benchmark performance did not guarantee open-world arena performance.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: InstructBLIP was fine-tuned on massive in-domain QA data and performed well on many existing tasks, but the authors found that it generalized poorly in the open-world arena.
04_failure_modes.correction: The authors complemented quantitative benchmarks with LVLM Arena, an open-world anonymous human preference evaluation.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: The online arena initially supported only single-round chats.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: High computational and memory demands prevented multi-round chat support at the time of reporting.
04_failure_modes.correction: The authors identified multi-round support as a future update for the LVLM Arena platform.
